sections.title: What changed in release 1.0.0 (2026-09-16)
sections.blurb: New pages, new data and fixes, from the changelog.
items: Added: Glossary: twenty canonical categories (mapped at load from the labels written across the data files), one regular category grid with an animation for every category, and a specific picture on every term that has one (its target's schematic, its molecule, its technology's schematic or the organ it concerns) in the table and at the top of the term page.

Added: Email signup: a SignupBox in the footer and on /newsletter/, driven by NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGNUP_ACTION (Buttondown or Listmonk form endpoint); until it is set the box offers the Atom feed and the per-page Watch button.
Added: Initials placeholder (RowAvatar) for startups, organisations and people without a usable logo or portrait; hotlinked favicons that fail or come back as the generic 16 px globe fall back to it.
Added: Journal wordmarks for Nature, the New England Journal of Medicine, Science and The Lancet from Wikidata via their Wikipedia titles, shown on the journals index and journal pages.

Added: Seventeen ChEMBL drug targets (SRC-family kinases, GM-CSF and IL-11 receptors, xanthine oxidase, DNA polymerase alpha, steroid, serotonin, dopamine, opioid and cannabinoid targets) with HGNC, UniProt and ChEMBL links.

Added: Six NCI-listed supportive-care drugs (eltrombopag, romiplostim, emapalumab, fostamatinib, ravulizumab, propranolol as Hemangeol) from FDA labels; the chlorambucil-prednisone regimen from the ECOG trial; six earlier Cancer Statistics reports as key papers.
Added: Papers for sixty-one leaders and OECI representatives via Europe PMC author and affiliation matching, each set checked against the person's role.
Changed: Provenance tags (gap-fill, chembl-gap, ctgov-ingest, nci-list and similar) are hidden from reader-facing pills and excluded from similarity scoring; they remain in the JSON API.
Changed: People pages show one plain-English provenance line under the papers table instead of a fetcher note on every row.
Changed: Table cells wrap long tokens site-wide; the models table's paper column uses short labels with the identifier as hover text.
Changed: Nine dead organisation websites replaced with verified current addresses; four Wikipedia links repointed to existing articles; every Wikipedia and organisation link in the corpus checked.
Changed: NCI drug list credits two-letter regimen acronyms; the completeness matcher no longer drops "AC".

Also in 1.0.0: work unreleased since 0.4.0: Molecule3D: ball-and-stick models of small molecules (CPK colours, shaded spheres, depth-sorted bond cylinders with double and triple bonds, drag to rotate, element legend) and smooth backbone ribbons for proteins (Catmull-Rom through the C-alpha trace, per-chain colours, wider on helices and strands, bound drug in ball-and-stick), with a wireframe toggle. Used on product pages, in every molecule thumbnail, and in a new "Solved structures with a drug bound" panel on target pages.

Also in 1.0.0: work unreleased since 0.4.0: PDB snapshots now keep secondary structure from the HELIX and SHEET records (ss); npm run fetch:structures -- --refresh-pdb 5A9U,5DK3 refreshes chosen entries without touching the rest.

Also in 1.0.0: work unreleased since 0.4.0: Startups and investors: company records gain optional stage, ycBatch, investors, funding (sourced rounds, amounts only where the source states them) and acquiredBy; companyType: "investor" for venture funds, corporate venture arms, an accelerator and disease foundations, whose portfolios are derived from backlinks.

Also in 1.0.0: work unreleased since 0.4.0: 62 Y Combinator companies attacking cancer, drawn from the open YC directory dataset and checked one by one (src/data/companies-yc.ts, snapshot with every hit and its decision in src/data/universe-lists/yc-oncology.json); 187 further venture-backed oncology companies across therapeutics, diagnostics, AI, digital care, radiotherapy hardware, surgery and tools (src/data/companies-startups.ts); 69 investors (src/data/investors.ts).

Also in 1.0.0: work unreleased since 0.4.0: /startups/ (stage strip, YC batch chips, filters by stage, modality, cancer, batch, investor and country, most active investors, recently funded) and /investors/; Funding panel on company pages, Portfolio panel on investor pages; stage and investor facets on /companies/; Startups and Investors in the Institutions & people group.

items: 2026-09-08 · Inhibrx claims first win for the long-sought OX40 target: Responses in head and neck cancer, strongest in HPV-positive tumours, after 15 years of failed OX40 programmes at big pharma. (Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, Immune checkpoint inhibitors)

2026-09-08 · A breakthrough pancreatic cancer drug won approval. Patients still struggle to access it: Insurance barriers after the daraxonrasib approval. (Daraxonrasib, Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma)

2026-09-08 · Metabolic syndrome commonly develops in men on ADT plus ARPI: About 40% within a year, per the reported analysis. (Androgen deprivation & AR pathway inhibitors, Prostate cancer, Cardio-oncology)

2026-09-08 · Azacitidine/venetoclax boosts event-free survival in induction-eligible AML: Coverage of the NEJM head-to-head with intensive chemotherapy. (Azacitidine, Venetoclax, Acute myeloid leukaemia)
2026-09-08 · Alcohol-attributable cancer mortality has doubled in the US since 1990: Prevention story with policy implications. (Chemoprevention & risk-reducing surgery)

2026-09-08 · DeLLphi-305: durvalumab + tarlatamab meets OS in first-line maintenance ES-SCLC: 563 patients; first phase 3 T-cell engager OS win in first-line maintenance small-cell lung cancer; numbers pending a congress. (Tarlatamab, Durvalumab, DeLLphi-305, Small-cell lung cancer)
2026-09-08 · Arlocabtagene autoleucel meets primary endpoint in the QUINTESSENTIAL myeloma trial: The GPRC5D CAR-T advances toward filing. (GPRC5D, CAR-T cell therapy, Multiple myeloma)

2026-09-07 · KEYLYNK-001: pembrolizumab ± olaparib maintenance in BRCA-wild-type ovarian cancer: Vergote et al., 7 September: the immunotherapy plus PARP maintenance question in first line. (Pembrolizumab, Olaparib, Ovarian cancer, PARP inhibitors)

2026-09-07 · Lessons from one of the first randomised trials of AI in medicine: Lång, 7 September: what the MASAI mammography-AI trial taught about running AI trials. (AI in radiology, Mammography & tomosynthesis)
2026-09-07 · Oncology dealmaking is becoming more surgical: Buyers target specific modalities and assets rather than platforms. (Antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), Radioligand therapy (beta emitters))
2026-09-05 · Six first-in-class approvals in August, including Etcamah: Camizestrant counted among August's first-in-class approvals. (Camizestrant)

2026-09-04 · Accelerated approval: camizestrant + CDK4/6 inhibitor for ESR1-mutated HR+/HER2- breast cancer: Etcamah approved 4 September after a 6-3 negative advisory vote, on SERENA-6 ctDNA-guided switching data. (Camizestrant, SERENA-6, Estrogen receptor (ERα), HR-positive / HER2-negative breast cancer)

2026-09-04 · Etcamah grabs FDA approval for advanced breast cancer with ESR1 mutations: Camizestrant plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor, accelerated approval. (Camizestrant, HR-positive / HER2-negative breast cancer)

2026-09-04 · Targeting fibroblast activation suppresses chemotherapy-induced pro-invasive remodelling: Stroma as a therapeutic target after chemotherapy. (FAP, Epithelial-mesenchymal transition & drug efflux)

items: 2026-09-17 · checkmate-548: One record named "CheckMate 548 & CheckMate 143 & CheckMate 498" carried a single registry id (NCT02667587, which is CheckMate 548 only) and yearReported 2020 for all three. They are three separate trials: CheckMate 143 (NCT02017717, JAMA Oncology 2020), CheckMate 498 (NCT02617589, Neuro-Oncology 2023) and CheckMate 548 (NCT02667587, Neuro-Oncology 2022). The glioma history also dated CheckMate 143 to 2017 while the record said 2020. (Reader report (neurosurgeon), checked against ClinicalTrials.gov and the PubMed records (143, 498, 548)) · split into checkmate-143, checkmate-498, checkmate-548, each with its own registry id, publication, year and outcomes; history entry moved to 2020

(Reader report (neurosurgeon), checked against PubMed (source)) · source set to https://doi.org/10.1093/neuonc/noac116
